full_judgment:
2. The plaintiff respondent Nos.1 to 8 filed Title Suit No. 126 of 1996 in the Court of the Assistant Judge, Muksudpur, Goplaganj for declaration of title in the suit land described in schedule to the plaint and for further declaration that the recording of the suit land in khas khatian No.1 in the name of the Government was wrong and illegal. 

 3. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, was that the suit land originally belonged to their predecessor Md. Bala Mia who used to possess the same personally. But in the R.S. khatian of the suit land the name of Md. Bala Mia was wrongly recorded as "middle interest holder" (মধ্য স্বত্ব ভোগী) instead of as tenant. That in view of this wrong recording in R.S. khatian the S.A. khatian also was prepared wrongly Showing the suit land as the khas land of the Government of khas khatian No. 1. That in the first part of Baishakh, 1403 B.S. when the plaintiffs went to local tahsil office for paying rent of the suit land they came to know about this wrong recording of the suit land for the first time. That the defendants also disclosed that they would lease out the suit land to others and also threatened the plaintiffs with dispossession and thus the plaintiffs were compelled to file the suit. 

 6. Mr. Mahabubey Alam, the learned Attorney General appearing for the petitioners has mainly argued that the High Court Division has erred in decreeing the suit without reversing the concurrent findings and decisions of the courts below; that the High Court Division did not take into consideration at all that the plaintiffs could not produce any material or evidence before the court to prove that their predecessor-in-interest was actually a raiyat in the suit land and that the recording of his name as "মধ্য স্বত্ব ভোগী" in the R.S. khatian has been wrong. The learned Attorney General has argued also that the R.S. khatian has a presumptive value and in the said khatian the status of the predecessor of the plaintiffs has been shown as "middle interest holder" and there was no material or evidence on record to rebut the presumptive value of the R.S. khatian and in the circumstances the High Court Division has committed wrong and illegality in decreeing the suit without making any clear finding as to the status of the predecessor of the plaintiffs with respect to the suit land. The learned Attorney General has argued also that the revisional court has committed wrong in declaring the plaintiffs title in the suit land only on the finding that the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit land. 

 II. Because the R.S. khatian having a presumptive value and in the said khatian the status of the predecessors of the plaintiffs having shown as holder of the intermediately interest and as there is no materials to rebut the said presumption, the High Court Division erred in decreeing the suit without arriving at any finding regarding status Of the predecessor of the plaintiff."
